props.gloss_en: the mishna: one may not soak asafoetida in lukewarm water
[dilemma: one who soaked (asafoetida), what?] Rav Adda of Naresh before Rav Yosef: one who soaked is liable to a sin-offering
Abaye's reductio: then one who soaked meat in water would also be liable? (asserted by no one)
Abaye: rather, [soaking asafoetida is forbidden] by rabbinic law
so that he not do [on Shabbat] in the way he does on a weekday
[R' Yochanan asked: may one soak asafoetida in cold water?] R' Yannai: it is forbidden
R' Yochanan's inference from the mishna: hence in cold water it is permitted
R' Yannai: the mishna is an individual's [view] -- R' Yosei's, per the baraita he cites
the baraita's first clause: one may not soak asafoetida in hot water
the baraita's first clause: nor in cold water
R' Yosei: in hot water it is forbidden
R' Yosei: in cold water it is permitted
what is it [soaked asafoetida] made for? for heaviness of the heart
Mar Ukva to Rav Acha bar Yosef: go drink three shekels of asafoetida over three days
he went and drank on Thursday and on Shabbat eve
a person drinks a kav or two kav [of it] and need not be concerned [the context: drinking it on Shabbat]
[Rav Acha: my dilemma is soaking.] Rav Huna: thus says Rav -- one soaks [asafoetida] in cold water and puts it in the sun
even per the one who forbids: that is only where he had not drunk at all
since he drank on Thursday and Shabbat eve, if he does not drink on Shabbat he is endangered
[Rav Acha asked Rav Safra: may one rub a linen shirt on Shabbat -- is it to soften, permitted, or to whiten, forbidden?] Rav Safra: he intends to soften, and it is permitted
Rav Safra: he intends to soften [not to whiten]

Rav Acha: about a scarf I had no dilemma, for I asked Rav Huna and he resolved it for me [the text says only ופשט לי; permissive per 140a.23's proposed inference, and per the Rif as Steinsaltz cites him]
Rav Chisda: this linen shirt -- pulling it off the reed is permitted
pulling the reed out of it is forbidden
Rava: and if it is a weaver's implement, it is permitted [to pull it out]
Rav Chisda: a bundle of vegetables, if fit for animal food, may be moved
and if not, it is forbidden
Rav: a hook for meat may be moved
Rav: [a hook] for fish is forbidden
Rav Ketina: one who stands in the middle of a bed is as if standing on a woman's belly
Rav Chisda: a Torah student buying vegetables should buy long ones -- a bundle is a bundle, and the length comes of itself
Rav Chisda: a Torah student buying reeds should buy long ones -- a load is a load, and the length comes of itself
Rav Chisda: a Torah student who has little bread should not eat vegetables, because they whet [the appetite]
Rav Chisda: I ate no vegetables in my poverty nor in my wealth -- in poverty because they whet [the appetite], in wealth because I said: where vegetables enter, let meat and fish enter
Rav Chisda: a Torah student who has little bread should not break [it] into slices
(parenthetical variant) Rav Chisda: a Torah student who has little bread should not break [bread]
why? because he will not do it generously
Rav Chisda: at first I would not break [bread] until I had put my hand into the whole vessel and found in it all I needed
Rav Chisda: one who can eat barley bread and eats wheat [bread] transgresses bal tashchit
Rav Pappa: one who can drink beer and drinks wine transgresses bal tashchit
and it is not so: bal tashchit of the body takes precedence
Rav Chisda: a Torah student who has no oil should rub himself with ditch water
Rav Chisda: a Torah student buying meat should buy the neck (unka), which has three kinds of meat
Rav Chisda: a Torah student buying a linen shirt should buy from Nehar Abba and whiten it every thirty days, so it serves him twelve months of the year -- and I am guarantor
what is kitonita? a fine class (kita na'a)
Rav Chisda: a Torah student should not sit on a new mat, for it ruins his clothes
Rav Chisda: a Torah student should not send his clothes to his host to whiten, for it is not proper conduct -- lest he see something on it and come to disgrace him
Rav Chisda to his daughters: be modest before your husbands; do not eat bread before your husbands
do not eat vegetables at night, do not eat dates at night, and do not drink beer at night
and do not relieve yourselves where your husbands relieve themselves
and when someone calls at the door, do not say 'who is he' (manu) but 'who is she' (mani)
he held a pearl in one hand and a clod in the other; the pearl he showed them, the clod he did not show them until they were distressed, and then he showed them
